::: {.why}
Four weeks of live paper trading is not enough to conclude anything and it is enough to be honest about, and the reporting standard you set today is the one the whole capstone rests on.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report the paper account's performance with every period included and no exclusions.
- State what a track record of this length can and cannot support, with the standard error attached.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Produce the track record table: monthly returns with no month omitted, cumulative return, realised volatility, maximum drawdown, and turnover. Then attach the Sharpe standard error at this sample length from qlib/stats.py, which will be wide enough that the point estimate carries almost no information, and say so on the same page rather than in a footnote.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Reconcile it against the broker: the account's own statements against your engine's derived positions and cash, using the day 327 reconciliation. Any difference that cannot be explained goes into the report as an unexplained residual rather than being absorbed into a rounding line.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the one-sentence statement of what this record supports, which is that the system runs and produces the positions it intends, rather than that the strategy works.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The live paper track record is reported with every period included and reconciled against the broker's own statements, with the Sharpe standard error at this sample length stated on the same page as the estimate.
:::
